en: Catalogue of Dharma Sought at Seiryō-ji Temple;
Catalogue of Dharma Sought by the Monk Enchin of Enryaku-ji Temple in the Capital of the Kingdom of Japan, five sheets in total;
comprising one hundred and fifteen fascicles of scriptures and other texts of the two divisions, Tāizō (Garbhadhātu) and Kongō (Vajradhātu).
The two mandalas along with their ritual implements, etc.:

*The Mahāvairocana Sūtra on the Attainment of Buddhahood*, one volume in seven fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha; *The Vajraśekhara Yoga Sūtra of Concise Recitation*, one volume in four fascicles, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi. These two works above are recorded in the Kaiyuan Lu.
*The Dharma Prohibition of One Hundred Transformations of Vajra Ucchuṣma*, one fascicle; *The Exposition of the Supernatural Dharmas by Vajra Ucchuṣma*, one fascicle; both translated by Āzhídá Sàn.

*The Original Text of the Mahākaruṇā-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara*, one fascicle; *The Samādhi Method of Vairocana from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, one fascicle;
*The Secret Method of the Dhāraṇī of Acala’s Messenger*, one fascicle; all translated by Vajrabodhi. *The Yoga Section on the Dharma of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, Part One.
*Mahāsukha-vajra-amogha-tattva-samaya-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Vajraśekhara-yoga-akṣamālā-sūtra*, one fascicle; both translated by Amoghavajra;
*Sarvatathāgata-vajrāyus-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle; co-translated by Vajrabodhi and Amoghavajra; *Ekākṣara-uṣṇīṣa-citrasūtra*, three fascicles;
*Vajra-bhairava-samāja-vaipulya-vidhi*, one fascicle; *Atiladara-aruli-li-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Mañjuśrī-stotra-dharmakāya-namaskāra*, one fascicle.

*The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Twelve Mudrās and One Hundred and Eight Names of the Auspicious Goddess Tārā*, one fascicle; *The Dhāraṇī of the Jewel Casket Seal of the Relics of the Entire Bodies of All Tathāgatas*, one fascicle;

*The Tattvasamaya Sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Ritual Manual of the Eleven-faced Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, three fascicles; *The Sūtra of the Twelve Epithets of the Auspicious Goddess Tārā*, one fascicle;

*The Index to the Eighteen Assemblies of the Vajraśekhara Yoga*, one fascicle; *The Dharma Gate of the Distinction of the Holy Ranks of the Vajraśekhara*, one fascicle; *The [Sūtra on] Bodhi...* [text fragment].
The *Cakrasaṃvara-tantra* (Vajraśekhara-rāja-sūtra) in five fascicles; the *Vajrāyuṣ-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in one fascicle; the *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-sūtra* in three fascicles;

the *Ritual for the Worship of the Tathāgata Amitāyus* in one fascicle; the *Mahāmegha-cakra-varṣaṇa-sūtra* in two fascicles; the *Dhāraṇī-sūtra for Bestowing [Relief upon] the Hungry Ghosts of the Flaming Mouth* in one fascicle;

and the *Bodhyalaṃkāra-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in one fascicle—these were all translated by Amoghavajra. The *Sukumāra-kumāra-paripṛcchā-sūtra* in either two or three fascicles was translated by Śubhakarasiṃha. (8)
*Mahābodhisattva-maṇḍala-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Pāṇḍaravāsinī-avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-sūtra*, one fascicle;
*Vaiśravaṇa-rāja-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Vajraśekhara-padma-kula-hṛdaya-japa-vidhi*, two fascicles; *Vajraśekhara-yoga-sahasrabhuja-sahasranetra-japa-vidhi*, one fascicle;
*Akṣobhya-tathāgata-japa-vidhi*, one fascicle; *Ekākṣara-uṣṇīṣarāja-japa-vidhi*, one fascicle; *Ekākṣara-uṣṇīṣarāja-yoga-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Buddhoṣṇīṣa-vijaya-dhāraṇī*.
*The Ritual Manual for Recitation*, one fascicle; *The Method for Recitation of the Vajraśekhara-uttaratantra-yoga*, one fascicle;

*The Method for Recitation of Vajrāyus*, one fascicle; *The Secret Sūtra for Recitation of Vajrarāja Bodhisattva*, one fascicle; *The Ritual Manual for Recitation of Samantabhadra-Vajrasattva*, one fascicle;

*The Ritual Manual for Recitation of Vajraśekhara-yoga*, one fascicle (alternatively titled *The Great Bliss Vajrasattva Benevolent Kings Prajñāpāramitā Recitation Method*); *The Method for Recitation of Cintāmaṇicakra*, one fascicle; *The Great Ākāśa...* [text fragment].
*The Method for Recitation in the Treasure [Collection]*, one fascicle; *The Ritual Manual for the Heart Mantra of the Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva*, one fascicle;

*The Method for Recitation of the Yoga Lotus Family*, one fascicle; *The Method for Recitation of Tārā Bodhisattva from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Yoga Method for Recitation of Amṛtakuṇḍalī*, one fascicle; *The Ritual for Receiving the Bodhicitta Precepts*, one fascicle;

*The Vajraśekhara Yoga Liturgy for the Thirty-seven Honored Ones*, one fascicle; *The Catalogue of Dhāraṇīs of All Families*, one fascicle; and *The Meaning of the Seventeen Honored Ones of the Great Maṇḍala*.
*Shu* (Explanatory Notes), one fascicle; *Saptakoṭibuddhamātṛkādhāraṇīsūtra*, one fascicle; *Siddhividhi of the Lotus Sūtra King*, one fascicle;
*Vajraśekhara-prathama-sādhana-vidhi*, one fascicle; or alternatively, the *Mahāsukha-vajrasattva-mahāyakṣa-priyaputra-siddhi* extracted from the *Yogatantra*;
or alternatively, the *Strī-harṣa* (also known as the *Hārītī-mātṛ-vidhi*); *Mahāsukha-vajra-amoghasatya-samaya-sūtra-artha-vyākhyā*, one fascicle; *Samantaprabhā*.
*The Sūtra of the Great Parṇaśavarī Dhāraṇī*, two fascicles; *The Verse on the Five-Syllable Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle; *The Method for Reciting the Holy Yamāntaka Wrathful King*, one fascicle;

*The Ritual Manual for Accomplishing the Greatly Majestic and Wrathful Ucchuṣma*, one fascicle; *The Ritual Manual for Accomplishing the Holy Krodha-Vajrakumāra Bodhisattva*, three fascicles; *The Sūtra of the Ekajaṭī Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle;
*The Ritual Manual for Reciting the One-Syllable Cakravartin King from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, one fascicle; and *The Exposition of Swift and Immediate Realization*.
*The Kinnara-Aveśa Dharma*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Mahāvairocana Tathāgata’s Attainment of Buddhahood: A Brief Exposition of the Seven-Limb Recitation and Practice*, one fascicle;

*The Brief Compendium of the Mahāvairocana Sūtra on Recitation and Practice*, also titled *The Essential Practice of the Five Limbs*, one fascicle; *The Great Ritual Manual of Vajraśekhara Trailokyavijaya*, one fascicle (alternatively, this may include the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara from the *Tattvasaṃgraha*);
*The Yoga Ritual Manual of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Vajraśekhara Sūtra: Contemplation of Self-* [text truncated].

*In the Life of King Ruru*, one fascicle; *The Maṇḍala of Mañjuśrī’s Constellations*, two fascicles—both translated by Amoghavajra; *The Treatise on the Three Aspects of the Bodhicitta of the Vajraśekhara*, one fascicle, compiled by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra;
*The Ritual Manual for the Cultivation of the Contemplative Practice of Prajñāpāramitā*, one fascicle; *The Commentary on the Śūraṅgama-samādhi Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle;

*The Method for the Recitation and Accomplishment of Avalokiteśvara’s Great Compassion*, one fascicle; and *The Sūtra of the Radiant Empowerment of Vajrapāṇi*, also titled *The Supreme Standing Mudrā*, one fascicle.
*The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Holy Acala*, one fascicle; *The Ritual Manual for the Painting Altar of the Great Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī*, one fascicle;

*The Essential Method for the Recitation of the Golden Wheel King Buddha-uṣṇīṣa*, one fascicle; and *The Method for the Great Holy Joyful Double-bodied Vināyaka*, one fascicle—these were all translated by Amoghavajra.

*The Yoga Recitation Method of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Cintāmaṇicakra*, one fascicle, translated by Vajrabodhi. *The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Vajraśekhara Yoga Samantabhadra Practice*, one fascicle, also titled *The Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven*.

A complete set of five copies of the ritual implements for the *Tattvārtha-maṇḍala* and other maṇḍalas, including the Great Vairocana Buddha Womb Realm (*Garbhadhātu*) Great Maṇḍala; one scroll and six copies of the nine-assemblies maṇḍala of the Great Vairocana Buddha’s Vajradhātu; and one set of six copies of the Great Vairocana Buddha Nine-Crested Wheel-Turning King (*Navamuṇḍa-cakravartin*) Maṇḍala. These two items above were entrusted by the Ajari Dengyō.

One scroll of the seed-syllable maṇḍala of the eighty-one deities of Mahāvairocana Buddha; four vajras for ritual action (karma-vajra); four ritual stakes for stabilizing the altar; and one scroll of the catalog for seeking the Dharma, including the aforementioned scriptures, dhāraṇīs, and Buddha images.

This has been transcribed and verified at the Qinglong Temple in Xinchang Ward, Left Street, Chang’an City, within the Great Tang Empire, under the presence of the Venerable Huichao, the Dharma-transmitter. It is hereby completed.
This brief catalog is provided as listed above.
Recorded on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month in the ninth year of the Dazhong era of the Great Tang by the monk Enchin, seeker of the Dharma.
The aforementioned maṇḍala, dharma-gates, and so forth,
were exclusively entrusted to the Upādhyāya,
who personally oversaw and verified them.
Each and every point is in accordance with the Dharma, with nothing differing; yet,
fearing that later students might harbor doubts or uncertainties, [I have written this].
I, [Name], prostrate myself.
Great Ajāri of the Dharma Transmission,
I beg you to graciously bestow upon me a name.
To serve as a perpetual testimony.
Submitted by the disciples of the Japanese National Teacher, the monk Enchin,
on the fifteenth day of the seventh month in the ninth year of the Dazhong era.
Having entered the Womb of Great Compassion (*mahākaruṇā-garbha*) and received the five-vase empowerment (*pañca-kalaśa-abhiṣeka*),
one becomes a Bodhisattva who has attained the *prajñāpāramitā*. Thereupon,
the training in the Great Teaching of the Womb (*garbha-mahā-śāsana*) is completed.
Furthermore, on the third day of the tenth month,
he entered the Vajradhātu Maṇḍala and received the five-family consecration,
thereby attaining the bodhisattva Vajrapāramitā.
He then conferred the training in the Vajradhātu Susiddhi and the yogas of the various deities;
having completed approximately one hundred volumes,
he arrived again on the fifth day of the eleventh month.
He entered the consecration mandala for the rank of Great Ācārya of the Five Divisions of the Mahāyāna Teachings and attained the status of a Maṇḍala Bodhisattva.
The aforementioned Venerable Enchin—
Having been granted the teachings of the supreme vehicle of the *dhāraṇī*,
he mastered them all; his eloquence in answering questions and explaining meanings was inexhaustible.
It may be examined and transmitted for preservation to widely benefit those with whom there is a karmic affinity;
this constitutes the distinction between the signs.
I pray to behold you in the Pure Land.
Take great care, take great care!
On the twenty-first day of the tenth month in the ninth year of the Dazhong era,
by the śramaṇa of the Qinglong Temple who transmits the teachings.
The Venerable Dharmaquan, who formerly resided at Changsheng Hall as a practitioner of recitation,
has sent this letter to Yuanzhen. May it be so, may it be so, a thousandfold, ten thousandfold.
